:::{#cor-question-information-bound}
#### An answer carries at most the logarithm of the number of possible answers

Let $A$ be the [answer](#def-answer) to a [question](#def-question) with $k$ [possible answers](#def-possible-answer)
about a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with finite [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy).
With base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm),
the [mutual information](#def-mutual-information) between $X$ and the answer is at most $\log_2 k$ [bits](#def-bit):

$$\mutinfof{X}{A} \le \log_2 k,$$

with equality exactly when the $k$ possible answers are equally likely.
For a [polar question](#def-polar-question), $k = 2$,
so the answer carries at most $1$ bit about $X$.

:::

::: {.proof}

Each [possible answer](#def-possible-answer) is a nonempty [set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-set) of values of $X$ with positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability),
so the answer $A$ has exactly $k$ values with positive probability,
and its [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) is finite.
By @thm-answer-information and then @thm-entropy-at-most-log-values,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mutinfof{X}{A}
&= \entropyf{A} \\
&\le \log_2 k,
\end{aligned}
$$

with equality exactly when $A$ is [uniform](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-uniform) on its $k$ values.
A [polar question](#def-polar-question) has $k = 2$ possible answers, and $\log_2 2 = 1$.

:::
